title: Marketing basics
examples: How does knowing my customer help me sell things?
What is the difference between a product and a brand?
Can you give an example of the four Ps in action?

explain.say: Today we are learning about marketing basics for businesses. We will look at the four Ps. These are the key elements of marketing.

draw.text: The Four Ps: Product, Price, Place, Promotion

explain.say: The first P is product. This is what the business actually sells. It could be a physical item or a service. For example, a bakery sells bread as its product.

draw.text: Product: The good or service offered

explain.say: Next is price. This is how much the customer pays for the product. Businesses must set a price that people are willing to pay. For example, a bottle of water might cost one dollar.
Place refers to where the customer can buy the product. This is about distribution. For example, a local bookstore might sell books in its own shop.

draw.text: Place: Where the customer buys it

explain.say: Promotion is how the business tells people about its product. This includes advertising and public relations. For example, a shoe company might run a television advertisement.
Understanding your customer is very important for marketing. You must know who you are selling to. For example, selling toys to young children is different from selling tools to builders.

draw.text: Customers: Who are you selling to?

faq.q: What is the main difference between a product and a service?
faq.a: A product is a physical item you can touch, like a phone. A service is an action or work done for you, like a haircut.
asks: Is a software program a product or a service?

faq.q: Why is setting the right price so difficult?
faq.a: The right price must cover costs but also attract buyers. If it is too high, no one buys it; if it is too low, the business loses money.
asks: How do I know what price to charge?

faq.q: Does 'Place' only mean a physical shop?
faq.a: No, 'Place' also means online availability. Selling through a website is a modern form of place.
Branding is the feeling people have about your business, not just the product itself. It is the reputation you build in people's minds.
asks: Is branding the same as a logo?
How do I build a brand?

faq.q: Which P is most important to start with?
faq.a: You must start with the customer and the product. If the product does not solve a real customer problem, the other Ps will fail.
asks: Should I think about promotion first?

facts: Marketing aims to satisfy customer needs and wants.
The four Ps are Product, Price, Place, and Promotion.
Branding is about the perception or feeling associated with a company.
A service is intangible, meaning it cannot be touched.

quiz.say: A company selling organic soap is changing its scent to attract people who prefer lavender. Which P is changing?
quiz.why: The scent is a feature of the soap, which is the product itself.

wrong.0: Changing the scent does not change how much the soap costs.
wrong.1: Changing the scent does not change where the soap is sold.
wrong.2: Changing the scent is a physical change, not just an advertisement.

quiz.say: A local cinema decides to only show films on weekends to maximize attendance. Which P is being adjusted?
quiz.why: Changing the operating days changes where and when the service is available.

wrong.0: This is a change in availability, not an advertisement.
wrong.2: The film itself is the product, not the showing schedule.
wrong.3: The cinema is not changing the ticket cost.

quiz.say: A soft drink company starts using famous athletes in all its advertisements. This is an example of adjusting which P?
quiz.why: Using athletes in ads is a marketing effort to raise awareness.

wrong.0: The ad does not tell us where to buy the drink.
wrong.2: The drink formula is not changing, only the promotion.
wrong.3: The price of the drink remains the same.
